correctness.rationale: The CDF directly gives the sampled survival. Differentiation yields the generalized-polynomial E with at most three positive roots counting multiplicity and two at y=1; hence the continuous hazard has the required monotone or single-minimum shape. Moving one-interval integrated hazards retain at most one trough. The sign identity is exact, and H(lambda) has one derivative sign crossing with limit log(alpha/theta), implying a unique p threshold precisely when theta<alpha<1. Analytical proof covers every parameter and infinitely many steps; 378 numerical grid cases and 2,584 exact rational sign identities were additional checks.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest literature supplies strong premises. Its continuous hazard theorem combined with the discrete construction does not itself provide the all-integer no-extra-turning result, the exact initial hazard discriminator, or the uniqueness of a p crossover for theta<alpha. The proof adds the integrated-hazard lemma and a separate one-crossing result for H(lambda). This is a nontrivial but closely related refinement, not an unrelated new model.

originality.rationale: The original discrete UGDGE law and earlier continuous Marshall-Olkin hazard classification are explicitly acknowledged. The sharp integer-sampling resolution threshold and complete resulting discrete sequence phase do not appear in inspected relevant primary full text or published mathematical records. The result is a close extension with known-input premises and an acknowledged indirect-coverage risk, not a claim that its continuous hazard classification was unknown.
residual_risks: The 2015 continuous hazard result plus standard flooring identities are close antecedents; future exhaustive literature inspection could reveal an equivalent discrete sampling corollary.
The journal final version of the 2018 paper was checked through metadata and the arXiv full text, not every publisher-hosted page.
Published research searches and additional overlap comparisons are non-exhaustive and cannot certify global uniqueness.

value.rationale: A unique, explicit p-resolution boundary tells when discretely observed reliability data must conceal an underlying bathtub-shaped failure rate. The result classifies all admissible parameter values of a published geometric-maximum count model, with an infinite-sequence no-extra-turn theorem and a practical one-step algebraic discriminator. It is neither a routine moments calculation nor an arbitrary unmotivated numerical slice.
